name: Scaling, load balancing and decoupled messaging

lesson.summary: Scalability is the ability to handle more load by adding resources, and elasticity is adjusting resources up and down as demand changes. EC2 Auto Scaling adds and removes instances within a minimum and maximum size, and Elastic Load Balancing spreads incoming traffic across them. Decoupling parts of an application with messaging services such as SQS, SNS and EventBridge keeps one slow or failing part from bringing down the others.
keyPoints: Scalability is the ability to handle a larger load by adding resources, scaling up (bigger) or out (more machines)
Elasticity is adjusting resources up and down dynamically as demand changes
EC2 Auto Scaling adds and removes instances between a minimum and a maximum size to match demand
Auto Scaling groups keep a minimum number of instances running, and you pay only for the instances that run
Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming traffic across instances, which can sit in several Availability Zones
Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing work together: Auto Scaling changes the number of instances and the load balancer routes traffic to them
Tightly coupled components fail together; loosely coupled components communicate through messages
Amazon SQS holds messages in a queue until a consumer processes and deletes them
Amazon SNS sends one message to many subscribers (publish-subscribe)
Amazon EventBridge routes events, such as an order placed, to the services that need them

scenarios.text: An online food delivery service receives a burst of orders at dinner time. A payment step, a restaurant notification step and a delivery step must all happen for each order, and the payment step is sometimes slow.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes elasticity in AWS?

options.text: Permanently increasing capacity once for long-term growth
Growing and shrinking resources automatically as demand changes
Buying fixed hardware that never changes size
Manually changing the instance type each month

questions.explanation: Elasticity means resources grow and shrink automatically as demand changes. Scalability is the broader ability to handle more load, and the other options describe fixed or manual capacity.

questions.prompt: In an EC2 Auto Scaling group, what does the minimum capacity setting define?

options.text: The most instances the group can ever run
The least number of instances kept running
The instance type used for every new instance
The number of Regions the group can use

questions.explanation: Minimum capacity is the fewest instances the group keeps running. The maximum is the upper limit, the instance type is set by the launch configuration or template, and a group works within a single Region.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of Elastic Load Balancing?

options.text: To distribute incoming traffic across multiple resources such as EC2 instances
To store customer files in buckets
To send billing reports to customers
To write application code automatically

questions.explanation: Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming application traffic across targets such as EC2 instances, improving performance and availability. The other options describe different services.

questions.prompt: Match each AWS messaging or routing service with what it does.

pairs.right: Holds messages in a queue until they are processed
Sends one message to many subscribers
Routes events, such as an order placed, to other services

questions.explanation: SQS is a queue, SNS is publish-subscribe fan-out, EventBridge routes events between services, and Elastic Load Balancing spreads traffic across instances.

questions.prompt: Which design best stops a slow payment step from holding up the whole food delivery flow?

options.text: Put every step in one tightly coupled service so they fail together
Send the events for each order through a message service so the other steps continue independently
Stop accepting orders whenever payment is slow
Store each order on a laptop until payment finishes

questions.explanation: Decoupling with a message service such as SQS or EventBridge lets each step work from its own queue, so one slow step does not stop the others. Tight coupling spreads failures, and stopping orders or local storage are not reliable designs.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Auto Scaling changes the number of instances as demand changes
Elastic Load Balancing spreads incoming traffic across the instances
The two services have no relationship and cannot be used together
Elastic Load Balancing creates new Regions when traffic rises

questions.explanation: Auto Scaling adjusts the instance count and Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic across them, and they work together. Load balancers do not create Regions, and the two services are designed to be used together.

questions.statement: Auto Scaling charges you for every instance in the group, even the ones that are not running.
questions.explanation: False. You pay for the instances that run, so Auto Scaling avoids paying for idle capacity.
